paragraphs: In [Sotah 38b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.38b.15), Ada teaches in the name of Rabbi Simlai. In [Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 10:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Terumot.10.6.8), Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman says in the name of Rabbi Yonatan, “Ada, our colleague, testified before us concerning sixty.” Hyman compares [Chullin 98a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.98a.10), where Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi and the authority designated רש״בג in the supplied Hebrew both transmit a teaching in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi. It appears to Hyman that the Jerusalem Talmud SHOULD READ רש״בג in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: “Ada, our colleague, testified.”[^4]

notes.text: The supplied רש״בג does not cleanly match the complete Chullin98a paragraph, which explicitly names Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani with Yaakov bar Idi. It is not expanded as Shimon ben Gamliel here. The source’s reporting initials and the proposed Yonatan-to-Yochanan change remain open.

The saved whole Davidson Chullin 98a paragraph explicitly names Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi and Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani, both reporting Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: an egg at sixty is forbidden, at sixty-one permitted. This is a concrete candidate comparison for supplied רש״בג, not proof of a gimel/nun error history. The siglum remains visible and is not expanded as Shimon ben Gamliel. The Terumot Yonatan-to-Yochanan change is Hyman's separate SHOULD READ proposal, not a newly adopted identity. Uninspected Sotah/Jerusalem Talmud abbreviated titles remain R'; the three inspected Chullin title occurrences support full Rabbi locally.

Both occurrences of the abbreviation in Hyman’s printed notice appear to read רש״בנ, with nun. The supplied Hebrew has רש״בג, with gimel. Chullin 98a names Yaakov bar Idi and Shmuel bar Nachmani in the report from Yehoshua ben Levi. The preceding report there has a separate Idi bar Idi bar Gershom chain. In Terumot 10:6, Shmuel bar Nachman transmits the statement about colleague Ada in Yonatan’s name. A preceding statement there names Shimon bar Abba and Yochanan. Hyman’s proposed reading of the Ada statement is a conjecture.

The [Seder HaDorot entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=236&lang=en) records the Sotah transmission from Rabbi Simlai. The linked Terumot paragraph gives Rabbi Yonatan for this testimony. Rabbi Yochanan occurs earlier in a separate report. The linked Chullin passage names Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani alongside Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi.
